full_judgment:
Mr. A. K. M. Sadeque, J: This Rule was issued calling upon the Deputy Commissioner, Sherpur and opposite party No. 1 to show cause as to why the order dated 29.3.93 passed in Special Tribunal Case No. 34 of 1992 by the Sessions and Senior Special Tribunal Judge. Sherpur should not be set aside and also why the custody of Rashida Begum should not be given to her father Md. Faizal Haque and also why the Special Tribunal Case No. 34 of 1992 Should not be withdrawn from the Court of the Senior Special Tribunal Sherpur and transferred to Senior Special Tribunal Jamalpur or any other Senior Special Tribunal. 

 2. The victim girl Rashida Begum was a witness in Special Triburial Case No. 34 of 1992 under Sections 366/109 of the Penal Code read with section 4(b) of the Cruelty to Women (Deterrent Punishment) Ordinance, 1984 by her father Md. Faizal Haque against accused Alal, Billal, Awal, Quddus, Amir Hossain and Safir Member in which charge sheet was submitted under the said section against the accused including Alal and his father Nurul Islam. It was alleged in the F.I.R. that the victim girl who was a minor forcibly kidnapped by the aforesaid accused. The victim girl Rashida Begum Made statement under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure before the Thana Magistrate, Nokia on 25.9.92 supporting the F.I.R. allegation of her being kidnapped for the purpose of marrying of accused Alal. Medical report dated 28.9.92 was to the effect that victim Rashida Begum was aged between. 16/17 years. The present petitioner prayed for getting custody of his daughter and the learned Magistrate allowed the prayer by his order dated 25.9.92. Thereafter the learned Magistrate by his another order dated 18.11.92 sent the case record to the Court of the District and Sessions and Special Tribunal Sherpur for trial. 

 3. The learned Special Tribunal Sherpur received the case record on 30.11.92 for trial and fixed 18.4.93 for framing the charge. Thereafter on 29.3.93 victim girl Rashida Begum appeared in the court of the learned senior Special Tribunal Sherpur and prayed for being given to the custody of accused Nurul Islam the father of accused Alal whom she claimed to be her husband. The learned Special Tribunal by his impugned order allowed the victim girl Rashida Begum to go to the custody of accused Nurul Islam on the grounds that she was aged between 16/17 years and that she had told the court that she had married the accused Alal on her own volition and that she after a reflection of two hours in his presence expressed her desire to remain in the house of accused Nurul Islam where she had already gone. The learned Senior Special Tribunal allowed the victim girl Rashida Begum to go to the house of accused Nurul Islam father of accused Alal upon his execution of a bond of Tk.5000/- undertaking to produce her before the court as on when necessary. 

 5. There was an initial objection to the application on the ground that the rest of the accused in this case were not made parties in the application and no order can be passed to their prejudice at least with regard to the prayer for transfer which should, be an independent Misc. case under section 526 of the Criminal Procedure Code. Being faced with this objection Mr. Abdur Rab-1 the learned Advocate for the petitioner has abandoned the prayer for transfer of the case. 

 6. It is submitted by Mr. Abdur Rab-1, the learned Advocate that this case being one under section 4(b) of the Cruelty to Women (Deterrent Punishment) Ordinance, 1983 the age of the victim girl could be of no consideration because under section 4(b) of the Ordinance one is guilty of the offence if one kidnaps or abducts a woman and so the age of the victim girl will of no consequence in considering whether she should be allowed go to the custody of her choice. 

 7. It appears that victim girl Rashida Begum initially in her statement under section 164 Cr.P.C. on 25.9.92 supported the prosecution case that she was abducted forcibly but subsequently she stated before the learned Sessions Judge that she had willingly married the accused Alal and she is willing to stay in the house of accused Nurul Islam the father of accused Alai where she had already gone. The learned Sessions Judge allowed Rashida Begum to stay in the house of accused Nurul Islam father-in-law of the girl particularly because he found that in the matter of her custody her choice should receive due regard since she was found by the doctor to be between 16 and 17 years on 23.9.92. 

 The Rule is accordingly discharged. The Senior Special Tribunal should however conclude the trial of the case within three months from the date of receipt of this order.
